title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the surrounding pages. X and Y are smooth projective varieties over an algebraically closed field k, with n = dim X. A_X and A_Y are their Albanese varieties, with Albanese maps φ_X : X → A_X and φ_Y : Y → A_Y. Z is an algebraic cycle of codimension n on X×Y.

Theorem 1.1 (on earlier pages) attaches to Z a homomorphism of abelian varieties u_Z : A_Y → A_X. It is characterised by the identity S_X(ᵗZ(𝔑)) = u_Z(S_Y(𝔑)) for 0-cycles 𝔑 of degree 0 on Y. Here S denotes the Albanese summation map on degree-0 zero-cycles, and ᵗZ(𝔑) is the transported 0-cycle on X.

The previous page reduces this identity to Lemma 1.4. It does so through the duality A_X ≅ A_X^** = B^* (B = Pic^0(X)), comparing images under Θ in Pic^0(B). Lemma 1.4 in turn follows from Lemma 1.5, an equality of divisor classes on B obtained by intersecting with a divisor D linearly equivalent to Θ.

This page does three things:
(1) It dismisses the proof of 1.5 as standard intersection theory.
(2) It passes to the ℓ-adic cohomological viewpoint. The cycle class γ^n(Z) ∈ H^{2n}(X×Y, Z_ℓ)(n) defines, by the usual correspondence formula α ↦ pr_{Y*}(pr_X^*α ∪ γ^n(Z)), a degree-preserving map a(γ^n(Z)) : H^1(X) → H^1(Y). It is degree-preserving because codim Z = dim X.
(3) It states Theorem 1.6: the square formed by a(γ^n(Z)) on top, u_Z^{(1)} = (u_Z)^* : H^1(A_X) → H^1(A_Y) on the bottom, and the canonical pullbacks φ_X^*, φ_Y^* as verticals commutes. The verticals are called 'isomorphisms (mod torsion?)'. Coefficients are Z_ℓ.

In modern terms this is the compatibility of the Albanese functoriality of correspondences with the action of correspondences on H^1. H^1(X, Z_ℓ) ≅ Hom(T_ℓ Alb_X, Z_ℓ) ≅ H^1(A_X, Z_ℓ). Hence the action of Z on H^1 is the transpose of T_ℓ(u_Z).

The next page draws the consequence (Cor. 1.7). For abelian varieties X and Y, a map H^1(X) → H^1(Y) comes from a codim-n cycle iff it is u^{(1)} for a homomorphism u : Y → X. Moreover u is determined by Z and is independent of ℓ. This is the classical identification of correspondences modulo divisorial ones with Hom of Albanese/Picard varieties (Weil), read cohomologically.

The purpose of the whole section is to pin down the 'H^1 part' of the standard/Lefschetz/Tate conjectures, where everything is known through abelian varieties.
errors: The verification of Theorem 1.6 is only asserted ('on vérifie sans difficulté'). It is in fact routine: H^1(Y, Z_ℓ) is torsion-free, so commutativity can be checked after ⊗Q_ℓ. There it reduces to the definition of u_Z via the Albanese map and the identification H^1 = dual of T_ℓ.

Implicit hypotheses are not stated on this page: k algebraically closed and ℓ ≠ char k. The canonical maps φ^* are in fact isomorphisms on H^1 with Z_ℓ coefficients (not merely mod torsion), because H^1(X, Z_ℓ) = Hom(π_1^ab, Z_ℓ) kills torsion. The hedge '(iso. mod torsion ...)' is therefore unnecessary.

Variance needs care. u_Z goes A_Y → A_X, matching the identity S_X(ᵗZ(𝔑)) = u_Z(S_Y(𝔑)), so that u_Z^{(1)} : H^1(A_X) → H^1(A_Y) is a pullback. This is consistent, but sign and transpose conventions are not specified.

ideas.what: Action of an algebraic correspondence of codimension dim X on ℓ-adic H^1 via its cycle class
ideas.modern_name: Correspondence action / cycle class map in étale cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 4½ cycle class, Standard Conjectures framework)
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles (1969); SGA 4½ (Deligne, cycle class)

ideas.what: Compatibility of the Albanese homomorphism u_Z induced by a correspondence with its action on H^1 through the Albanese map (Thm 1.6)
ideas.modern_name: Albanese functoriality of correspondences; H^1(X,Z_ℓ) ≅ H^1(Alb X, Z_ℓ) ≅ T_ℓ(Alb)^∨
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil, Lang (Abelian Varieties); folklore in motives (Kleiman, Scholl: h^1 of a variety is h^1 of its Albanese/Picard)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the discussion of the Lefschetz/Hodge-type conjectures in degree 1 in 'Standard conjectures'; not as a numbered statement as far as known

ideas.what: Corollary (next page): for abelian varieties, cycle-induced maps on H^1 are exactly those induced by homomorphisms, with u independent of ℓ
ideas.modern_name: Hom(A,B)⊗Z_ℓ ↪ Hom(T_ℓA,T_ℓB) and algebraicity of H^1-correspondences; degree-1 case of Tate/Hodge for products
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (correspondences and Hom of Jacobians/Albanese); injectivity in Tate/Lang

deep.surprise_reason: The page states a standard compatibility, between the Albanese homomorphism induced by a correspondence and its action on ℓ-adic H^1, whose proof is routine and well known. The only mildly interesting element, a relative version over an arbitrary base using K-theoretic cocycles, appears on the next page, not here.
transcription_corrections: 'Suivant des point de vue cohomologie l-adique' should read 'Suivant du point de vue cohomologique ℓ-adique' (i.e. 'Following, from the ℓ-adic cohomological viewpoint, the construction just made').

In the parenthesis after 'applications canoniques' the manuscript reads roughly '(iso. mod torsion ...?)' with a second illegible line, possibly 'si ℓ ≠ p'. The transcription's '[?]' is appropriate, and the word after 'mod' is crossed out/overwritten.
The final crossed-out line is 'Ce diagramme est commutatif' (struck through), correctly rendered as deleted.
